  "text": "The library’s return slot caught anything thicker than a paperback. Martin kept a ruler beside the desk to push the books through.

On Tuesdays, a woman returned gardening books wrapped in supermarket bags.

“In case it rains,” she said.

He unwrapped them carefully and gave the bags back.

One afternoon she brought a book about apple trees. A leaf lay between pages forty and forty-one.

“Yours?” he asked.

She looked at it.

“Not anymore.”

He set it beside the date stamp.

The following Tuesday, she arrived without books.

“Have you got anything on growing things in pots?”

He showed her the shelf. She chose a thin volume with a cracked spine and stood reading it near the radiator.

“Less digging,” she said.

At closing time, Martin found the leaf beneath his sleeve. He put it inside an old dictionary behind the desk.

For several weeks she borrowed books about balconies, herbs, small spaces. Then she brought him six tomatoes in a margarine tub.

“They’re not very big.”

“They don’t need to be.”

He ate two with his sandwiches and took the others home.

In November, the return slot was replaced. The workman asked whether Martin wanted the ruler thrown out.

“No,” he said. “We use that.”

He put it in a drawer.

The woman came late that afternoon, carrying a damp paperback beneath her coat.

“Forgot my bag.”

Martin fetched one from the cupboard. While she packed the book, he asked about the tomatoes.

“Finished now. I’ve put bulbs in.”

She folded the spare handles inside her pocket.

“Something to look at in March.”"
